sections.title: Alike and different
sections.content: Say that two people are alike with *is … is*: *Anna is, Meg is szemüveget visel.* (Both Anna and Meg wear glasses.) Say that they differ with *de*: *Anna magas, de Meg alacsony.* To correct a wrong idea, use *nem … hanem …*: *Anna nem alacsony, hanem magas.* *Károly nem fehér inget visel, hanem kék inget.*

items.english: Both Anna and Meg are tall.
Anna is tall, but Meg is short.
Anna is not short, but tall.

items.spanish: Károly nem fehér inget visel, hanem kék inget.
items.english: Károly doesn't wear a white shirt, but a blue shirt.

items.spanish: Meg is, Anna is szemüveget visel.
items.english: Both Meg and Anna wear glasses.

sections.content: *Hanem* only follows a negative part: *nem alacsony, hanem magas*. For a simple contrast with no *nem* use *de*.
